facts.fact_text: The first to third applicants, together with other concerned residents, formed the fourth applicant to campaign against the City of Sunderland College's proposal to build on the Arena.

The first to third applicants, together with other concerned residents, formed the fourth applicant to persuade the Council not to grant the City of Sunderland College permission to build on the Arena.
On or around 14 March 1998, the first applicant, together with her husband and son, set up two stands at the entrance of the shopping mall in the Galleries.
The stands set up by the first applicant on or around 14 March 1998 displayed posters alerting the public to the likely loss of the open space known as the Arena.
The stands set up by the first applicant on or around 14 March 1998 were used to seek signatures to present to the Council on behalf of Washington First Forum.
Security guards employed by Postel Properties Limited would not let the first applicant or her assistants continue to collect signatures on any land or premises owned by Postel Properties Limited.
The applicants had to remove their stands from the Galleries.
The applicants had to stop collecting signatures at the Galleries.
In his reply of 14 April 1998, the manager of the Galleries refused the third applicant access to the Galleries and adjacent car parks.

The fourth applicant produced a list of associations and others which were given permission to carry out collections, set up stands and displays within the Galleries.
The Salvation Army was given permission to carry out a collection before Christmas within the Galleries.
Local school choirs were given permission to carry out carol-singing and a collection before Christmas within the Galleries.
The Stop Smoking Campaign was given permission to set up an advertising display and hand out nicotine patches within the Galleries.
The Blood Transfusion Service was given permission to carry out a blood collection within the Galleries.
The Royal British Legion was given permission to carry out a collection for Armistice Day within the Galleries.
Various photographers were given permission to carry out advertising and taking of photographs within the Galleries.
British Gas was given permission to set up a staffed advertising display within the Galleries.
Sunderland Council was allowed to use the Galleries for the 'Your Council, Your Choice' consultation campaign.
